sections.title: Headline
sections.content: A preregistered study finds pluralistic AI agents can amplify diverse public input on AI policy, recovering most of the satisfaction and fairness gap versus single-model input, though direct human participation remains preferred.

sections.title: Scaling public input on AI policy with pluralistic agents
sections.problem: AI deployment spans many cultures and stakeholder groups, but gathering diverse public input for AI policy is hard to scale.
sections.method: Pluralistic agents (AI representatives that deliberate for individuals) were tested in computational experiments and a preregistered study with 746 human participants, comparing pluralistic-agent deliberation against single-AI input and direct human discussion.
sections.key_result: Agents shifted policies toward represented personas, with influence depending on persona instructions (verbosity and lower cooperativeness increased influence); pluralistic-agent deliberation was rated more useful and fair than single-AI input, recovering 68% of the satisfaction gap and 82% of the fairness gap versus direct discussion, though direct human participation was preferred overall.
sections.caveat: The authors recommend cautious use as an amplifier of human input, not a replacement; agent influence was sensitive to persona instructions.
sections.why_it_matters: It offers an empirical, preregistered test of whether AI agents can broaden participation in AI policy while flagging limits relative to direct human deliberation.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The single selected paper reports a preregistered human study showing pluralistic AI agents can partially close satisfaction and fairness gaps versus single-model input. Direct human participation was still preferred, and the authors frame agents as an amplifier of human input rather than a replacement.
